model: behaviour: RandomForestClassifier on the 10 objective features (synthetic, survey-grounded labels)
protocol: Data and split identical to ml/ablation_studies.ablate_behavior(): generate_behavior_dataset(25000, seed 42) (28,750 rows incl. boundary blends), objective-10 features, stratified 80/20 train_test_split(random_state=42). Replication gate: the deployed config must reproduce the ablation-table test accuracy within 0.002. Full 120-config grid, 5-fold StratifiedKFold(shuffle, seed 42) on the 23,000 training rows only, with StandardScaler+RF in one Pipeline (scaler refit per fold). Selection by mean CV macro-F1 (ties go to grid order). Test set (5,750 rows) scored once for the deployed and once for the CV-best config. Paired bootstrap of best - deployed: 1,000 test resamples, seed 42, via ablation_studies.boot_ci. Survey check afterwards (selects nothing): both configs scored on the IGDS9-SF respondents exactly as ml/eval_behavior_survey.py scores the served model, with the served isotonic recipe refit in memory.

cv.scheme: StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42) on the 23,000-row training split only

cost.note: fit times on 23,000 rows with 16 threads

survey_check.question: Does the CV-best forest's gain on simulated labels transfer to real people? Construct validity on the IGDS9-SF survey (it validates meaning, not clinical accuracy).
survey_check.data: data/survey/responses.csv (gitignored): respondents kept by ml/eval_behavior_survey.py's filter (adult, current gamer, attention check, complete IGDS9-SF) with complete Q5-Q11 answers
survey_check.scoring: eval_behavior_survey.objective_features (Q5-Q11 band midpoints) -> derive_psychometrics -> StandardScaler -> RandomForest -> isotonic layer (ml/calibrate_behavior.py recipe refit in memory: CalibratedClassifierCV(FrozenEstimator(rf), method=isotonic) on the calibration half of the held-out simulator split, random_state 7) -> b = 0.5 P(Some concern) + 1.0 P(High concern); Spearman rho with the IGDS9-SF total

bootstrap.ci_from: eval_behavior_survey.bootstrap_rho per model; its index stream replayed for the paired difference

diagnostic_uncalibrated_rf.note: raw forest probabilities, no isotonic layer; diagnostic only

survey_check.conclusion: The decisive real-data test is the IGDS9-SF survey: scored exactly as ml/eval_behavior_survey.py scores the served model, the CV-best forest's score correlates with the IGDS9-SF total of the 103 scored respondents at Spearman rho 0.295 [0.115, 0.456], against 0.317 [0.137, 0.478] for the deployed forest: paired difference -0.022, 95% CI [-0.073, +0.027]. The CI includes 0, so the simulator gain is not shown to transfer to real people; at n = 103 the survey cannot tell the two forests apart, and the point estimate favours the deployed forest.

conclusion: Across 120 RandomForest configs, 5-fold CV macro-F1 on the 23,000 training rows spans 0.9057-0.9291 (median 0.9230). max_depth is the main lever: its marginal means differ by 0.0155, every other hyperparameter's by at most 0.0041. The deployed config scores 0.9221 +/- 0.0025 (rank 69/120, outside one standard error of the best) and the CV-best (n_estimators=200, max_depth=None, min_samples_leaf=1, max_features=sqrt) scores 0.9291 +/- 0.0024. On the 5,750 untouched test rows, accuracy is 0.9273 for the best config vs 0.9160 for the deployed one: paired difference +0.0113, 95% CI [+0.0063, +0.0165], best > deployed in 100.0% of 1,000 resamples. That is a real but small gain of +1.13 accuracy points on the simulator's held-out rows. It is reported, not adopted: switching means re-validating the served model, re-running the fairness audit and re-checking the device/backend budget (pickled model 1965 KB -> 46931 KB). The macro-F1 difference is +0.0107, CI [+0.0059, +0.0157]. Behaviour labels come from the survey-grounded simulator, so any gain measures fit to the simulator, not to real children. The decisive real-data test is the IGDS9-SF survey: scored exactly as ml/eval_behavior_survey.py scores the served model, the CV-best forest's score correlates with the IGDS9-SF total of the 103 scored respondents at Spearman rho 0.295 [0.115, 0.456], against 0.317 [0.137, 0.478] for the deployed forest: paired difference -0.022, 95% CI [-0.073, +0.027]. The CI includes 0, so the simulator gain is not shown to transfer to real people; at n = 103 the survey cannot tell the two forests apart, and the point estimate favours the deployed forest. The deployed model is unchanged.
